parts:
Hello,

 

With this data frame: 

 

     X   DM   DI   DL   VM   VI   VL

1   r1  2.7  6.8  6.5  2.5  7.3  5.0

2 r2.5  2.7 10.8 10.5  2.7  8.5 10.2

3 r2.5  9.5 16.5  9.7  7.3 13.2 10.7

4   r3 13.2 42.7 20.7  9.2 26.0 20.0

5   r4 17.7 49.2 27.5  6.3 35.7 26.5

6   i1 36.2 40.3 30.2 10.0 37.0 19.5

7   i2 52.0 34.2 20.3 34.0 36.0 25.5

8   i3 45.0 58.0 25.3 29.3 49.2 32.7

9   c1 32.3 44.3 16.2 23.5 42.7 22.3

 

I want to plot values in the X variable in the sequence indicated in the data.frame.  However, when I use the ggplot syntax, the values for the X variable are plotted in alphabetical order.  Is there a simple way to override this default?

 

xplot = ggplot(jenn, aes(X, DL))

xplot + geom_point()

 

Thanks,

 Art

messages.author: 4c2460918214ec91
messages.subject: Re: Basic question about data orientation along x axis
parts:
Hey Art-

this is typically dealt with prior to using ggplot, by some specifications to factor().

i'd do this, assuming jenn is your data frame

jenn$X.orig=jenn$X
jenn$X=factor(jenn$X.orig, levels=c( *your order here* ) )

Hope that helps. You can ?factor for more options. ggplot then respects these attributes of the factor in the frame.

best,

James

messages.subject: Re: Basic question about data orientation along x axis
parts:
Hi Art,

The easiest trick (I think) is to just (re)factor the variable so that
the order of the levels corresponds to what you want (in this case,
the same order as they appear). Here is example code:

## Read your data in
jenn <- read.table(textConnection("

9 c1 32.3 44.3 16.2 23.5 42.7 22.3"), header = TRUE)
closeAllConnections()
str(jenn)
levels(jenn$X)

## Graph
ggplot(jenn, aes(X, DL)) + geom_point()

## factor so that levels are in order, not alphabetical
jenn$X <- factor(jenn$X, levels = jenn$X, labels = jenn$X)

levels(jenn$X)
## New Graph
ggplot(jenn, aes(X, DL)) + geom_point()


Cheers,

Josh

Hi Art,

Unfortunately, you cannot quite use your "X" column as the rownames
(as in mtcars) because it is not unique. One of the requirements (in
R) for rownames is that they be unique. For example, if you asked for
row "r2.5", which one should R give you? Say you made them unique
using r2 and r2.5, the following would work:

## Read your data in
jenn <- read.table(textConnection("

## overwrite default rownames
rownames(jenn) <- jenn$X
jenn <- jenn[, -1] # 'remove' column 1, "X"

## A possible plot
ggplot(jenn, aes(DM, DL, colour = rownames(jenn))) +
geom_point() +
scale_colour_hue(name = "Rows")

## at this point, you can access specific rows via indexing (see ?"[" )
jenn["c1", 2:4] # row "c1" columns 2 through 4

Cheers,

Josh

Adam, 

Should work just fine.  You just define the levels of your factor and then plot. Because you're faceting by one factor and then reorganizing another as well you won't see b1 before a1 unless region b is before region a.
tst<-data.frame(region=c("a","a","b","b","b","c"),district=c("a1","a2","b1","b2","b3","c1"),percent=c(.1,.3,.2,.25,.35,.23))

tst$region<-factor(tst$region, levels=c("c", "a", "b"))
tst$district<-factor(tst$district, levels=c("b1","a2","b3","b2","a1","c1"))

ggplot(tst,aes(percent,district))+ 
geom_point()+ 
facet_grid(region~.,scales="free",space="free")+  
opts(legend.position="none")+

scale_x_continuous(formatter="percent")       #scale_y was incorrect

#B

tst<-data.frame(region=c("a","a","b","b","b","c"),district=c("a1","a2","b1","b2","b3","c1"),percent=c(.1,.3,.2,.25,.35,.23)) 
tst$region<-factor(tst$region, levels=c("c", "a", "b"))
tst$district<-factor(tst$district, levels=c("b1","a2","b3","b2","a1","c1"))

ggplot(tst,aes(percent,district))+ 
geom_point()+ 
facet_grid(region~.,scales="free",space="free")+  
opts(legend.position="none")+ 
scale_x_continuous(formatter="percent")       #scale_y was incorrect

#B
